LESSON: VISUAL DISCRIMINATION

Grade: PP2
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: READING
Topic 3.4: Visual discrimination

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Visual discrimination. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Match and pair pictures and objects at home and at school.
2. Take pleasure in visual discrimination activities at home and at school. Core-competence developed: Communication and collaboration, learning to learn, critical and creative thinking for problem solving.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. Match and pair pictures and objects at home and at school.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to match and pair pictures and objects at home and at school. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. Take pleasure in visual discrimination activities at home and at school. Core-competence developed: Communication and collaboration, learning to learn, critical and creative thinking for problem solving.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to take pleasure in visual discrimination activities at home and at school. Core-competence developed: Communication and collaboration, learning to learn, critical and creative thinking for problem solving. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Visual discrimination.
2. Explain Visual discrimination to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Visual discrimination.
4. Show that you can: Match and pair pictures and objects at home and at school.
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Visual discrimination. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Visual discrimination important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. Match and pair pictures and objects at home and at school.
2. Take pleasure in visual discrimination activities at home and at school. Core-competence developed: Communication and collaboration, learning to learn, critical and creative thinking for problem solving.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
